a: Common types include addition, substitution, elimination, and rearrangement.
Nucleophiles donate electrons; electrophiles accept electrons.
Chiral molecules are not superimposable on their mirror images.
Addition polymers form by adding monomers without byproducts.
Condensation polymers form with loss of small molecules like water.
Lock-and-key and induced-fit models describe enzyme-substrate binding.
A pairs with T; G pairs with C in DNA.
In RNA, A pairs with U; G pairs with C.
Primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary describe protein structure.
